newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium opens counselling line for crash witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Belgium opens counselling line for crash witnesses.

text.p: The Belgian Red Cross opened a special phone line on Wednesday to give trauma counselling to witnesses and members of the families of the victims of Saturday's crash at an air show in the port of Ostend.

Nine people were killed and more than 50 injured when the plane piloted by the leader of the Jordanian air force display team spun out of control and smashed into a crowd of people around a Red Cross tent near the runway at Ostend airport.
The telephone line will operate between 0900 and 2100 (0700 GMT and 1900 GMT). The numbers are 02/264.42.91 (92, 93, 94) or fax 02/264.42.95.
Captain Amr Hani Bilal, 28, of Jordan's Royal Falcons display team, was buried with military honours on Monday in Amman's royal cemetery.

Jordan's Queen Noor will arrive in Belgium on Thursday night to pay condolences to the families of the eight other people -- six Belgians and two French, including a 22-month-old girl -- who were also killed in the crash and ensuing fireball.
On Friday, Belgian Princess Astrid will attend the funeral service of a 19-year-old Red Cross volunteer who was among the dead.
The following day, there will be a memorial service for all the victims of the crash. Queen Noor is due to attend.
Thousands of Belgians have already filed past the coffins of the victims and signed a condolences register.
Belgium has opened an investigation into the crash, captured on film by an amateur video. The preliminary report is due on August 15.

Interior Minister Johan Vande Lanotte has refused to speculate on whether the crash was caused by human or mechanical failure, although it is clear that the plane broke air show rules and flew over the crowd.
A partial autopsy was performed on Bilal before his body was flown home, and the wreckage of his German-made Falcon XT 300 aerobatics plane is being examined by experts.
Belga news agency said on Wednesday the autopsy of Bilal had found no trace of intoxicants nor of any physical ailment or illness. No official confirmation was immediately available.
There have been numerous calls for air shows at civilian airports to be banned in Belgium, which has stringent safety rules. So far there has been no official response.
Air shows are popular events in Belgium each summer, regularly attracting tens of thousands of people.
